ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Act on Reporting and Use of Specific Financial Transaction Information (Act No. 16565, as amended); Criminal Proceeds Concealment Control Act (Act No. 16561); Enforcement Decree of the Act on Reporting and Use of Specific Financial Transaction Information; Commercial Act (Act No. 172, as amended) and the Registration of Corporations Rule; Real Name Financial Transactions Act (Act No. 16631, as amended).

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization by a licensed Korean notary public, then Apostille issued by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Korea under the Hague Apostille Convention of 1961.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing (Tax Payment and Good Standing Certificate)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National Tax Service of South Korea
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Apostille by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Korea, preceded by a certified true copy notarization of the executing tax officer's signature.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution and Power of Attorney (Including notary certification)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: The company itself, notarized by a Korean notary public
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization of the Corporate Seal and director signatures, followed by Apostille from the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Korea; no consular legalization required as Korea is an Apostille member state.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registered with the Seoul District Court, certified extract by the court registry
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Court-certified copy notarized by the court registry officer and then Apostilled by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Korea.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter (Korean Commercial Bank Account Confirmation)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: KB Kookmin Bank, Shinhan Bank, or other Korean commercial bank
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization of the bank officer's signature, followed by Apostille from the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Korea; no consular legalization chain is permitted.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: All Ultimate Beneficial Owners, directors, and authorized signatories must be screened against the OFAC Specially Designated Nationals List, the UN Security Council Consolidated Sanctions List, and the Korean Financial Intelligence Unit (KFIU) designated list. Screening must include politically exposed persons (PEPs) and their close associates/family members, with enhanced due diligence requiring senior management approval, source-of-wealth verification, and adverse media review. Re-screening is mandatory upon any name, address, or ownership change, and full audit trails must be maintained for at least five years after business relationship termination.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Supreme Court of Korea Internet Registration Office (IROS) for name search and reservation, administered by the local District Court Registration Division
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Under the Commercial Act and Court Registration Rules, the name must be in Hangul and must include the legal form designation 'Yuhan Hoesa'. A foreign-language name may be registered as an alias through phonetic transliteration into Hangul, but the primary registered name must be in Hangul. The four-tier naming convention requires (1) the corporate form, (2) the specific trade name, (3) a business purpose statement, and (4) a distinguishing number or device when the name is similar to an existing entity. Any non-Korean script must be transliterated into Hangul phonetically and may be appended as an alias in parentheses.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon a name rejection, the applicant must submit a written objection to the Registration Division of the local District Court within 14 days, attaching the IROS search result and proof that no identical or confusingly similar name exists in the same line of business. The court must issue a written certificate of allowance or final rejection within 7 business days. If rejected again, the applicant can petition the High Court through a formal administrative suit under the Administrative Litigation Act. The entire appeal may be filed through the IROS e-filing system, with all supporting evidence translated into Korean.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: The Commercial Act mandates a physical office address in Korea. A virtual office or commercial mailbox can be registered for media/PR businesses, but the National Tax Service and Korean banks apply a strict substance-over-form analysis. Where no staff, business equipment, or client-facing activity is located at the address, the NTS may reject business registration and banks will refuse corporate account opening. Therefore, a virtual office is permissible only when accompanied by a lease agreement, utility bills, and a qualified local resident agent for tax notices; without these, it is a serious red flag and may also invalidate the Korean corporate registration.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Inspection readiness checklist: (1) nameplate/business sign at the registered address, (2) local employment records and four major social insurance enrollment, (3) client service contracts and invoices, (4) board minutes and capital contribution proof, (5) bank account statements and checkbook, (6) tangible assets such as computer, phone line, and office furniture. The unannounced inspection risk is quantified at 15% during the first year for a low-risk PR firm, but increases to 45% if a virtual office is used without any physical staff presence.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Official court service fee schedule in KRW converted at 1,330 KRW/USD

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Apostille fees for 5 documents issued by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Korea
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: MOFA apostille service fee, KRW 2,000 per document (approx. USD 1.5 each)

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea (Act No. 1000, as amended), Chapter VII (Limited Liability Company, Yuhan Hoesa), Articles 287-2 through 287-74, together with the applicable provisions of the Registration of Real Estate Act concerning commercial registration and the Local Tax Act concerning registration tax; the incorporation of a Yuhan Hoesa is governed by these provisions rather than the stock company provisions.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Commercial Registration Division of the District Court having jurisdiction over the company head office (for example, Seoul Central District Court), with online filing available through the Korean Court Registration Information System (IRO)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Registration of Incorporation of a Limited Liability Company (Yuhan Hoesa), accompanied by the certified Articles of Incorporation and supporting governance instruments
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-in capital is prescribed for a Yuhan Hoesa. The Articles of Incorporation must state the subscribed capital amount. Cash contributions must be deposited into a blocked capital subscription bank account in the Republic of Korea, and the bank must issue a certificate of deposit confirming the paid-in capital before the registration application is submitted. The deposited funds remain blocked and may not be withdrawn for corporate operations until the court issues the Certificate of Registration of Incorporation. In-kind contributions, if any, must be described and valued in the Articles in accordance with the Commercial Act.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLUTIONS OF THE FIRST MANAGERS MEETING (PRO-FORMA) OF YUHANGHOESA, a Yuhan Hoesa (limited liability company) organized under the Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea, adopted by the unanimous written consent of the sole member and all initial managers as of [DATE], at the registered head office located at [ADDRESS]. WHEREAS the company was formed for the purpose of conducting international media relations, overseas public relations, crisis communications and advisory services within ISIC 7310; and WHEREAS the initial member has subscribed for the paid-in capital and the Articles of Incorporation have been executed; and WHEREAS the Commercial Act and the Articles of Incorporation require the company to confirm its capital subscription, approve bank arrangements, adopt a registered office and appoint statutory officers before the incorporation registration is lodged. NOW, THEREFORE, it is RESOLVED as follows: 1. SHARE CAPITAL SUBSCRIPTION. The initial paid-in capital of the company is fixed at [KRW AMOUNT], and the subscription made by the initial member is ratified and confirmed as fully paid and credited to the company. 2. BANKING AUTHORIZATION. The managers are authorized on behalf of the company to open bank accounts at [BANK], to execute bank account forms, to apply the corporate seal, and to appoint authorized signatories. All disbursements shall require the joint signature of any two authorized managers, unless varied by a subsequent resolution of the member. 3. REGISTERED OFFICE ADOPTION. The registered head office of the company is adopted as [ADDRESS], and the managers are directed to register that address with the competent District Court and the tax authorities. 4. APPOINTMENT OF STATUTORY OFFICERS. [MANAGER A] is appointed as the managing manager and representative business executor, [MANAGER B] is appointed as joint manager, and [AUDITOR NAME] is appointed as statutory auditor if required by the Articles or the Commercial Act. The managing manager shall have authority to execute all documents and to complete all government filings, tax registrations, and banking arrangements necessary to make the company operative. 5. POST-REGISTRATION AUTHORIZATION. The managing manager is directed to file the incorporation registration, obtain the corporate business registration certificate, release the blocked capital account, and perform all acts required to commence lawful operation. All resolutions contained herein are effective immediately and shall remain in full force until revoked by the member or managers in accordance with law. This pro-forma resolution is submitted solely as a model and must be adapted to the company actual parties, capital, date and address.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Pre-registration preparation, trade-name search and execution of Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Korean Court Registration Information System (IRO) and the Commercial Registration Division of the District Court for the planned head-office district
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a trade-name search and conflict check through IRO to confirm the proposed Yuhan Hoesa name is available. Prepare the Korean-language Articles of Incorporation in an English-Korean parallel format, stating the company name, business purpose, head-office address, capital amount, contribution type and valuation, manager details and governance provisions. Verify identity and residential status of each member and manager; for a foreign member or manager, obtain a certified passport translation and, if resident, a foreign resident registration certificate. Execute the Articles before capital deposit. If notarization is required by the registry or the bank, arrange notarization at the next step. Assemble the full dossier including IDs, powers of attorney, lease documents, and name search report. The Articles must comply with the applicable Yuhan Hoesa provisions of the Commercial Act to avoid correction orders.
required_dossiers: Proposed Articles of Incorporation
Passport or national ID of each member and manager
Foreign resident registration certificate for resident foreign managers
Power of attorney if using an agent
Trade-name search report or reservation confirmation
Head-office lease agreement or title evidence
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the trade-name search or draft Articles are rejected or queried, amend the name and text and re-submit through IRO within 5 business days. If the name is unavailable, select the secondary reserved name and re-execute the Articles.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening of blocked capital subscription account and deposit of paid-in capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: A licensed commercial bank in the Republic of Korea, normally the bank selected by the forming attorney
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary corporate capital subscription account in the name of the company or the proposed registered name. Each member deposits the subscribed cash contribution into this blocked account in accordance with the Contribution provisions of the Commercial Act. The bank issues a balance certificate confirming the aggregate paid-in capital. To comply with Korean foreign-exchange reporting, international wire transfers must state the subscriber name and corporate purpose; amounts over USD 5,000 require a bank-generated foreign-exchange transaction declaration. The account is blocked so that funds cannot be withdrawn until the completed company registration certificate is presented to the bank. Any in-kind contribution must be separately appraised and described in the Articles; cash-only companies need only the bank certificate.
required_dossiers: Executed Articles of Incorporation
Trade-name reservation evidence
Passport/ID and foreign-exchange declaration forms for international transfers
Bank account opening application and corporate seal
Bank certificate of deposit/balance certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank refuses to issue the deposit certificate due to KYC concerns, cure by supplying a notarized power of attorney and certified passport translation, or open the account at another licensed bank. The deposit step may be renewed without court penalty as long as the registration filing deadline under the Commercial Act is met.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarization of Articles of Incorporation and execution of governance documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Korean notary public or a law office with notarial commission, acting under the Korean Notary Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: If notarization is required by the District Court, bank, or legal practice, present the executed Articles to the notary. The notary verifies the identity, legal capacity and signatures of all members and managers; foreign signatories must present passports and alien registration certificates, together with authenticated translations where necessary. The notary affixes a notarial certificate recording the date and place of execution. Simultaneously, execute the member's meeting consent and manager acceptance letters. Confirm that the capital stated in the notarized Articles matches the bank balance certificate. The resulting certified file becomes the backbone of the registration application. Any discrepancy between the notarized capital and the bank certificate must be resolved before moving to Step 4.
required_dossiers: Executed Articles of Incorporation
Passport/ID of all members and managers
Alien registration certificate of resident foreign managers
Power of attorney for the applicant
Draft minutes of the first managers meeting and manager acceptance letters
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary objects to a provision in the Articles, amend the Articles by obtaining member signature and re-submit to the same notary within 3 business days. If the notary requires additional identity proof for foreign parties, provide a notarized English translation and, where beneficial, an apostilled passport copy.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Commercial registration of incorporation with the District Court
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial Registration Division of the District Court with territorial jurisdiction over the head office; filing through IRO or in-person counter
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the official Application for Registration of Incorporation of a Limited Liability Company together with the notarized Articles, bank balance certificate, head-office lease evidence, identity records and power of attorney. The registration officer examines whether the corporate purpose, capital, manager appointments, and address satisfy the Commercial Act. Once accepted, the court assigns a company registration number and issues the certificate of registered information. The capital escrow account can then be released upon presentation of the registration certificate. Thereafter, the company must complete tax registration with the National Tax Service within 14 days. The date of completion of this registration is the legal birth date of the company, and all pre-registration contracts executed in the company name must be ratified in the first board/managers meeting.
required_dossiers: Application for company registration
Notarized Articles of Incorporation
Bank certificate of paid-in capital deposit
Head-office lease agreement or ownership certificate
Member and manager resident registration abstracts or equivalent ID certificates
Power of attorney for the filing agent
Court fee payment receipt
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the court issues a correction order or suspension notice, supply the requested corrected document or explanation within the correction period, which is normally 10 to 15 days. If the registration is refused, prepare a fresh application package with corrected Articles and re-file, paying the applicable registration tax and surcharge again.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-registration tax registration, business license issue and bank mandate activation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) through Hometax, the competent district tax office, and the selected commercial bank
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within 14 days of court registration, file the business registration application with the NTS using the company registration certificate, Articles, lease contract, and bank account details. The NTS will issue a business registration certificate bearing the corporate tax ID. Then open the permanent corporate bank account and close or convert the temporary capital subscription account. Notify the Korea Employment and Labor agencies if employees will be hired. Because the company is a pure public-relations and communications firm under ISIC 7310, no industrial or environmental operating license is required; the ordinary business registration is sufficient. The managing manager should retain copies of all registrations and update the corporate governance book.
required_dossiers: Company registration certificate
Certified copy of Articles of Incorporation
Business registration application in Hometax
Head-office lease contract and landlord business registration certificate
Bank account opening certificate
Manager and member ID certificates and resident registration abstracts
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the NTS queries the address or foreign ownership structure, amend the Hometax application electronically and provide the court-certified company registration certificate and the head-office lease. If the bank will not activate the permanent account, present the NTS business registration certificate and the court registration certificate; late penalties are avoided by completing tax registration before the 14-day statutory deadline.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not Applicable - pure media relations, public relations and communications advisory service under ISIC 7310; no physical manufacturing, chemical, assembly or warehousing operation.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not Applicable - no statutory industrial operating license required for a public relations and communications firm; the company need only hold a general corporate business registration certificate issued by the National Tax Service.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Not Applicable - ISIC 7310 is a service-sector scope outside the EIA, full environmental impact report, and environmental registration categories under the Korean Environmental Impact Assessment Act and the Act on the Registration and Evaluation of Chemicals.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not Applicable - the firm has no industrial wastewater discharge, volatile organic compound emissions, point-source air emissions, or hazardous waste generation profile requiring quantitative permits or monitoring.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not Applicable - no physical production, chemical handling or warehousing that would require civil defense fire permits, structural load inspections or specialized occupational clearance. Standard workplace health and safety obligations under the Occupational Safety and Health Act and the Commercial Lease Agreement for the office remain applicable.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax Service (NTS), Ministry of Economy and Finance; online portal: HomeTax (www.hometax.go.kr). Export and customs declarations are processed through Korea Customs Service (KCS) on the UNI-PASS portal.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign non-resident establishing KR_YUHANGHOESA must (i) incorporate the Yuhan Hoesa under Korean commercial law and obtain the corporate registration number from the court registry; (ii) within 20 days after commencement of business, file a Business Registration Application with the district tax office of the National Tax Service through HomeTax and receive the 10-digit Business Registration Number, which is the single entity tax identification number for corporate income tax and VAT; (iii) where the foreign parent has no Korean place of business, appoint a domestic tax representative under the Framework Act on National Taxes and complete the non-resident taxpayer registration using the foreign corporate ID through HomeTax; and (iv) if cross-border goods are exported, register with KCS on UNI-PASS and obtain a customs clearance user code linked to the Business Registration Number. The business registration certificate, power of attorney, articles of incorporation, director identification and lease or ownership evidence of the registered place of business are the statutory supporting documents.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. Korea does not provide a check-the-box or hybrid mismatch pass-through election for a Yuhan Hoesa; it is mandatorily taxed as a domestic corporation under the Corporate Income Tax Act.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value-Added Tax (VAT) under the Value-Added Tax Act of the Republic of Korea
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No revenue-based VAT registration exemption for corporate businesses; a Yuhan Hoesa must apply for Business Registration through HomeTax upon commencement even if initial turnover is zero. For a non-resident supplier of cross-border digital or offshore services, Korean-sourced supplies to Korean businesses or consumers trigger non-resident VAT registration without any turnover threshold.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: E-invoicing is mandatory for all business-to-business VAT supplies. The supplier must issue an electronic tax invoice in the NTS HomeTax electronic invoice system by the 10th day of the month following the taxable supply month; the system issues a digital audit stamp and approval number. There is no separate real-time fiscal device pre-clearance requirement, but invoices must be transmitted to NTS electronically, and cancellation or correction requires a blocking or rejection code under NTS rules.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating is available for goods physically exported from Korea after an export declaration accepted by Korea Customs Service, and for services supplied to non-resident persons in the course of earning foreign exchange, including overseas public relations and communication-agency services, as long as the recipient is outside Korea and the consideration is collected through a Korean Foreign Exchange Bank. The offshore digital-services zero rating requires the foreign recipient to have no Korean place of business and the payment to be received in foreign currency; the claim must be supported by the service contract and foreign-exchange receipt.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Korea Customs Service Export Declaration Receipt (Export Declaration Confirmation) issued on UNI-PASS for physical exports
Transport evidence: Ocean Bill of Lading or Air Waybill and any required cargo manifest
Foreign Exchange Transaction Confirmation or Inward Remittance Voucher from a Korean Foreign Exchange Bank, evidencing receipt and purchase of foreign currency export proceeds
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: If export zero-rating is claimed without the statutory documentation, NTS will retroactively deny the 0% rate and assess VAT at 10%, with national-tax additional surcharges of up to 40% for unjustified or fraudulent refunds and 20% for negligent underreporting, plus late-payment interest and penalties for false e-tax invoices under the Value-Added Tax Act. False customs declarations are also subject to fines or imprisonment under the Customs Act, and failure to repatriate export proceeds within the statutory deadline may trigger penalties under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act. The tax statute of limitations is generally five years and is extended to ten years for fraudulent or non-arm’s-length transactions.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Korea (BOK) acting jointly with the Ministry of Economy and Finance (MOEF) as the Foreign Exchange Administration under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: South Korea maintains a heavily liberalised but strictly supervised foreign exchange system. Current account receipts and payments for services such as international media relations, retainer fees, royalties and reimbursed expenses are generally free to move across borders without approval, provided the underlying trade is evidenced and the transaction is handled by a licensed foreign exchange bank. Capital account items are less liberalised: inbound equity injection, capital increase, shareholder loans and profit repatriation are subject to BOK reporting, beneficial ownership declarations and tax withholding verification. The Korean won is not freely deliverable offshore, so no non-bank intermediary can execute true KRW clearing outside the domestic banking system. In practical treasury terms, the corporate must open a main KRW operating account at a domestic bank, convert foreign inward remittances at market rates, ensure that all outward remittances carry correct foreign exchange purpose codes, and preserve source documents for at least five years. Dividend or liquidation proceeds can be transferred out only after the bank has confirmed the existence of cumulative investment registration, payment of capital gains tax if applicable, and notarised board approval.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Export service proceeds are required to be collected within six months from the invoice or service-performance date. Under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act, there is no per-transaction fixed surrender percentage; rather, 100% of export receipts must be repatriated and cleared through a licensed foreign exchange bank. The bank will credit the amount to a foreign currency export account or automatically convert it to KRW. In the absence of a separately approved foreign currency export account, the receiving bank applies a de facto 100% KRW conversion at the bank's market rate. If a pre-registered foreign-currency treasury account is used, the entity can retain the foreign currency for forward hedging, but every subsequent FX conversion must be reported in BOK's FX information system.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Foreign Currency Export Proceeds Account and Operational Settlement
Capital Escrow Account and Trade Service Settlement

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low and legally constrained. Under the Korean Foreign Exchange Transactions Act, only institutions licensed as foreign exchange banks by the Financial Services Commission may execute KRW cross-border settlements and corporates fund transfers. Offshore digital EMIs such as Wise, Revolut Business, Airwallex and Currencycloud operate as e-money institutions outside that licence and are not eligible to settle through BOK-Wire+ or provide full KRW current accounts to Korean-resident legal entities. The Korean LLC must rely on at least one Tier-1 domestic bank account for KRW clearing, capital operations, trade disbursements and FX hedging. An offshore EMI may be used only as an ancillary non-KRW collection lockbox for clients in limited corridors without SWIFT access, never as the primary treasury rail.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For a newly formed Korean LLC, a branch-level KYC interview is effectively mandatory for at least one statutory director or a duly evidenced attorney-in-fact. Face-to-face verification remains the baseline even for low-risk public relations firms; some banks may permit remote video e-KYC when the director holds a valid Alien Registration Card and the bank's digital channels support it, but such treatment is discretionary and cannot be assumed. Korean consular proxy account opening is not generally accepted, because the bank must inspect the corporate seal certificate, the board resolution and the registered title of the authorised signatory. The compliance committee will require a clear source-of-funds story, identification of all non-resident shareholders and a two-year business plan evidencing real Korean operating substance.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial ownership opacity: the LLC is fully foreign-owned and the ownership chain crosses more than one jurisdiction, with media and PR receivables generated outside Korea.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified corporate registry excerpt showing all shareholders and registered directors dated within 30 days; notarised and apostilled certificate of incorporation and articles of association; executed board resolutions and powers of attorney; tax identification numbers and passports for every direct and indirect beneficial owner; bank reference letters from each material investor.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Capital injection exceeding the statutory reporting threshold on incorporation or inconsistent with the projected cash flows of a PR agency.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Investment registration report filed with the receiving foreign exchange bank and transmitted to BOK; accountant's capital verification certificate; source-of-funds letters and six months of bank statements from the parent or investor; audited consolidated financial statements of the parent; board resolution approving the capital contribution.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Payment destination clustering to offshore media-buying, social platforms, or advertising technology vendors in higher-risk jurisdictions.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full vendor due-diligence pack including business registration, UBO registry extract, bank account confirmation letter, signed insertion orders or ad-rate schedules, third-party media schedules evidencing service delivery and internal sanctions-screening output.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident managers holding signature authority without formal employment, unpaid director compensation or nominee-held signing rights.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Korean employment or project-based service agreements and payroll records; director tax withholding filings; corporate seal confirmation certificate; minutes of the shareholders' meeting appointing the authorised signatory; registered lease agreement or virtual office contract evidencing Korean operational substance.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Non-resident shareholders must file the applicable equity investment report with the Bank of Korea through the chosen domestic foreign exchange bank before funds are received. The remitting parent transfers funds by SWIFT MT103; the domestic bank credits the inward USD or other permitted currency to the capital escrow account only after the wire contains a clear purpose classification of equity contribution, not trade invoice. The Korean external accountant then issues a capital verification certificate and the funds are converted into KRW at the bank's market rate and swept into the operating account. Every related wire must quote the same BOK transaction classification code and the entity's foreign-exchange report reference number so that later profit repatriation can be matched.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Recurring media retainers, agency invoices and vendor settlement outside Korea are executed via SWIFT MT103, with remittance details referencing the signed contract and invoice. Korean won payments to domestic vendors clear through BOK-Wire+ and the KFTC real-time settlement system. For high-value broadcast or event commitments, Korean banks can issue commercial letters of credit through SWIFT MT700, typically requiring a cash margin of ten to thirty percent. Documentary collections are permissible as a secondary rail for verified service transactions, at the bank's discretion and subject to the presentation of transport-free service certificates, invoices and signed acceptance notes.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: USD/KRW deliverable forward contracts up to twelve months matched to documented trade or service receivables and payables
Cross-currency swaps for long-term media procurement or financing contracts where the underlying exposure is demonstrable
Plain vanilla FX options provided the underlying exposure is evidenced and the option premium is within the board-approved treasury risk limit
Onshore currency and interest rate swaps with linear payoffs, subject to BOK reporting and the real-demand principle

Offshore non-deliverable forwards are generally not available to the Korean entity for hedging purposes; any offshore NDF usage by non-residents around the KRW would be treated as speculative and is not an authorised treasury rail for the local LLC

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Ordinary general meeting of members and approval of annual financial statements (balance sheet, income statement, retained earnings statement, cash flow statement and business report)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: No government filing is required; officers must keep the meeting minutes in the corporate minute book and the approved financial statements at the registered office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 3 months after the fiscal year-end; for a 31 December fiscal year, on or before 31 March
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to convene leaves the financial statements without member approval; directors may face administrative fines under the Commercial Act; persistent governance failure is weighed by the tax authority as an aggravating factor in compulsory collection, and a creditor may petition the court for dissolution, but this item alone does not automatically cause administrative strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax return and local income tax surcharge return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) through HomeTax; the local income tax surcharge is remitted with the national corporate tax settlement
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 3 months after the fiscal year-end; 31 March for calendar-year companies. If the NTS extension is obtained for return preparation, the extended return is due by 31 May, with the estimated tax payable settled on or before 31 March.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late or non-filing penalty of 20% of the unpaid corporate tax (aggravated to 40% for fraudulent understatement), local income surtax at 10% of the assessed corporate tax, and arrears interest at 0.03% per day, approximately 10.95% per annum. Continued delinquency empowers the NTS to seize bank accounts, freeze receivables, cancel the business registration and apply to the court for compulsory dissolution or strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Independent auditor's report and audited financial statements filed through DART, if the statutory audit threshold is exceeded
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial Supervisory Service (FSS) through the DART e-filing system; a signed copy must also be retained with the company's statutory registers
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 2 weeks after the ordinary general meeting approving the financial statements, and in any event no later than the statutory close of the ordinary meeting period, which is 31 March for a 31 December fiscal year, unless a valid extension has been obtained
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to appoint an auditor or to file the audit report triggers penalties under the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies, including criminal fines up to KRW 50,000,000 and imprisonment for wilful omission, supervisory directives from the FSS, and, in repeated or severe cases, compulsory dissolution from the corporate register.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual statutory register compliance review and minute book update
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: No external filing; registers are maintained at the registered office and governed by the corporate secretarial agent and directors
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Ongoing; a full written review and update must be completed by the date of the ordinary general meeting of members, and in any event no later than 31 March for a calendar-year company
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to maintain, or incorrect maintenance of, statutory registers is punishable by administrative or low-level criminal fines under the Commercial Act; defective registers can invalidate member-transfer or charge registrations against third parties and may support creditor applications for judicial dissolution if combined with broader insolvency.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Quarterly value-added tax returns, including the final quarterly and annual adjustment return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Quarterly cycle for a calendar-year company: Q1 by 25 April, Q2 by 25 July, Q3 by 25 October, and Q4 with the annual adjustment by 25 January
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late or non-filing surcharge of 10% of the unpaid VAT, or 20% for intentional non-payment, plus daily arrears interest of 0.03%; continued failure can trigger business registration cancellation, bank attachment, and court-ordered compulsory dissolution.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Foreign-invested enterprise status and change reports, where any member is a non-resident
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy through KOTRA and the Invest KOREA One-Stop Service
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual status reconciliation is performed with the corporate tax filing by 31 March; any change in foreign shareholding, foreign investor identity, foreign-investment amount, or transfer of membership interest must be reported within 30 days of the occurrence
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to report may cause loss of foreign-investment incentives, administrative fines, refusal of registry amendments for share transfers, and in serious cases cancellation of foreign-invested enterprise status; combined with tax non-compliance it can accelerate compulsory dissolution from the corporate register.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies, the Yuhan Hoesa LLC must appoint an independent auditor registered with the Korean Institute of Certified Public Accountants if: (a) total assets on the preceding fiscal year-end equal or exceed KRW 12 billion, approximately USD 9,000,000; (b) the company is designated as an external-audit company by the Financial Supervisory Commission because of public interest or creditor risk; or (c) the company voluntarily elects external audit under the Act. Revenue and employee headcount alone do not create a statutory audit trigger in Korea; however, lenders, overseas PR agency contracts, or a parent-company consolidation requirement may impose a contractual certified audit. For a company with total assets below KRW 12 billion, members may adopt an audit by consent, but that consent does not convert the engagement into a statutory audit.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Audit-mandated Korean companies apply Korean IFRS as endorsed by the Financial Services Commission. Non-audit-mandated Yuhan Hoesa may prepare statutory accounts under Korean GAAP, which is aligned with the Commercial Act and the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies. The financial statements and independent auditor's opinion must be expressed in Korean won and, if filed, submitted through the FSS DART system.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: South Korea does not impose a general stand-alone annual public UBO declaration on a private Yuhan Hoesa. Beneficial-ownership integrity is enforced transactionally: (i) any transfer of a membership interest must be recorded in the register of members before it can be asserted against third parties; (ii) under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act, a foreign-invested enterprise must notify the Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy through KOTRA within 30 days after any change of shareholding, foreign investor, or foreign-investment amount; (iii) if the company acquires real estate, the ultimate beneficial owner must be reported within 30 days of acquisition under the Real Estate Transaction Report Act; (iv) for anti-money-laundering compliance, up-to-date beneficial-ownership information must be maintained and made available to the Korea Financial Intelligence Unit and financial institutions in any transaction covered by customer due diligence rules. The register of members and foreign-investment change reports therefore function as the annual confirmation mechanism for Korean corporate law.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 900 - USD 3,200 per year for a Seoul or provincial registered office, Korean corporate secretarial agent, business registration compliance, and statutory register custody
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 5,000 - USD 25,000 per year for a small overseas communications and public relations firm if a statutory audit is triggered; voluntary audit for a small PR company is typically USD 4,000 - USD 12,000

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24% top national Corporate Tax Act Article 55 progressive rate (9% up to KRW 200m; 19% from KRW 200m to KRW 20bn; 21% from KRW 20bn to KRW 300bn; 24% above KRW 300bn) plus 10% Local Income Tax surcharge on the national corporate tax for a combined top effective marginal rate of 26.4%
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: General Korean tax incentives such as R&D tax credits under the Special Tax Limitation Control Act, small and medium enterprise investment/employment credits, and foreign-investment tax holidays under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act for qualifying technology-intensive businesses; a Korea domestic Yuhan Hoesa engaged in overseas PR communications will ordinarily not be entitled to a free-zone or patent box rate unless the entity separately develops qualifying copyrighted software or high-tech intangibles, in which case certain R&D credits may reduce the effective rate

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form No. 55 Corporate Tax Base and Tax Return (filed electronically through the National Tax Service HomeTax e-filing portal at hometax.go.kr), together with supporting financial statements, tax adjustment schedules, reportable international transaction schedules, and non-resident withholding reconciliation schedules
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual corporate income tax return; accompanied by semi-annual preliminary corporate tax prepayment filings for companies with prior-year corporate tax liabilities and by monthly/quarterly withholding returns for non-resident payments
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Annual return must be filed within 3 months after the end of the fiscal year (e.g., 31 March for a 31 December year-end), with an additional extension of up to 1 month available in certain circumstances for foreign-controlled or overseas-branch taxpayers; any tax shown due must be remitted by the same filing deadline

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 1 - Entity Identification and Non-Resident Shareholder Schedule
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name, business registration number, tax serial number, address of Korean head office, fiscal year-end, principal business code (ISIC 7310 / NAICS 541820), paid-in capital, and percentage ownership of every non-resident shareholder
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Mark YES to the non-resident shareholder declaration and complete the non-resident owner schedule. For a Korea-incorporated Yuhan Hoesa owned by non-residents, identify the tax residence country, tax identification number, ownership percentage, acquisition date, and any foreign tax treaty residence circumstance that will later be relied upon for dividend withholding reduction.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 2 - Revenue Reconciliation (Gross Retainer and Project Income)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reconcile total accounting revenue from global PR retainers, crisis communications, media buying, event production, licensing of PR materials, and incidental reimbursements against the ISIC 7310 business scope; enter adjustments from Korean GAAP/IFRS to taxable revenue
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Do not net intercompany or overseas expenses against gross revenue. Include Korean-source service revenue performed by domestic staff, and, for services performed partly outside Korea, allocate income according to the Korean corporate tax source rules. The overseas PR company must keep daily work logs, client contracts, and country-specific revenue allocation proof to counter NTS underestimation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 3 - Cost of Sales and Operating Expense Controls
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Enter wages, social security, rent, third-party subcontracting, overseas media purchase costs, research subscriptions, software, travel, communications, legal and audit fees, and bad debt deductions
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Payments to a non-resident affiliate for overseas PR subcontracting, media placement, or branding services are deductible only if the expense is ordinary, necessary, and supported by a true arm's-length transfer pricing file. If the Korean entity pays a non-resident without withholding the statutory 22% on deemed royalties or service income attributable to a Korean source, the expense may be disallowed and the unpaid withholding tax assessed with penalties.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 4 - Tax Adjustments, Non-Taxable Income, and Disallowed Expenditure
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report temporary and permanent differences: nondeductible entertainment, statutory allowable donation ceilings, depreciation differences, related-party interest disallowance, capital losses, bad debt reversals, and tax-exempt portfolio dividends
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Where the NTS recharacterizes excessive management fees to a non-resident shareholder as a constructive dividend, the management fee will be added back to taxable income and also treated as a dividend distribution subject to 22% withholding tax. The non-resident entry guidance is to ensure every intercompany charge is backed by contracts, service-delivery evidence, cost records, and an arm's-length benchmark.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 5 - Tax Base Computation and Loss Carryforward
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Compute taxable income after tax adjustments, deductible prior-year losses, non-taxable income, and small-corporation deductions; enter the net tax base before rate application
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim the loss carryforward deduction under Corporate Tax Act Article 13 only if the eligible losses are within the 10-year carryforward window and the original returns were filed timely. A foreign-controlled PR firm cannot bypass the 10-year rule through a merger, liquidation of a related entity, or assignment of losses to a new Yuhan Hoesa.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 6 - Progressive Rate Application, Local Surtax, and Estimated Prepayments
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Apply the 9/19/21/24% brackets; compute national corporate tax, then 10% local income tax on the national tax; subtract prior estimated tax payments and prepayments
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: No special preferential corporate rate applies merely because the owners are non-residents. For treaty-based foreign investment incentives under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act, attach the approval certificate and the five-year/50% reduction schedules; otherwise the default corporate tax and local surcharge must be entered.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 7 - Tax Credits, Foreign Tax Credit, and Incentive Claims
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Compute domestic tax credits for R&D, employment expansion, investment in facilities, electronic tax invoices, and foreign tax credits for Korean companies with overseas branches or foreign subsidiaries
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A Korean Yuhan Hoesa cannot use the foreign tax credit as a substitute for withholding tax on a dividend paid to its non-resident parent. Foreign tax credit documentation requires a tax receipt and tax residence certificate from the source country, and the credit is limited to the Korean tax attributable to that foreign-source income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 8 - Withholding Reconciliation for Non-Resident Outbound Payments
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report all dividends, interest, royalties, and certain fees paid to non-residents; specify the payment amount, statutory/treaty rate applied, FGN code, amount withheld, and remittance date
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Default rates are 22% aggregate (20% national plus 2% local) on non-resident dividends, interest, and royalties unless a treaty reduction is properly substantiated. Attach the taxpayer residence certificate, beneficial ownership certificate, shareholding period evidence for reduced dividend rates, and a Principal Purpose Test/limitation-on-benefits analysis. Do not enter a zero withholding rate merely because the recipient is a holding company; the NTS will require substance and beneficial ownership.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 9 - Reportable International Transactions and Transfer Pricing Schedule
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: List each cross-border related-party transaction: PR fees, royalties, cost recharges, management service fees, loans, and disposal of intangibles; describe the transfer pricing method adopted and attach the relevant Local File/Master File if triggered
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For each foreign related party, complete the arm's-length analysis with functional, asset and risk profiles, comparable selection, and margin indicators. If the Korean entity performs high-value overseas public relations functions using its own reputation and client network, a cost-plus of 1% on costs is highly vulnerable to recharacterization as abandonment of intangible value; maintain contemporaneous time sheets, budgets, marketing materials, evidence of staffing, and a substantive decision-making record.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Failure to file or false filing attracts a 20% penalty of the unpaid tax for non-filing and 10% of the understated tax for under-reporting under the Framework Act on National Taxes; late-paid tax is subject to a 0.03% per-day late payment surcharge; fraudulent evasion under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act Article 3 is punishable by imprisonment for up to 5 years or a fine of not more than three times the evaded tax, with aggravated imprisonment of up to 7 years when the evaded tax exceeds KRW 300 million; directors face criminal referral and the NTS may list the entity and responsible director on the tax-delinquent blacklist and impose an overseas travel ban.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 22% aggregate withholding on outbound dividends paid by a Korean Yuhan Hoesa to a non-resident corporate shareholder (20% corporate income tax under Corporate Tax Act Article 98 and 2% local income tax surcharge), reducible by bilateral DTA rates that are commonly 5% for shareholdings of at least 10% and 15% for portfolio dividends, with other negotiated rates before the applicable OECD MLI Principal Purpose Test
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke treaty relief, the payer must obtain from the non-resident recipient a Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) issued by the resident country's tax authority, a signed beneficial ownership statement, and evidence of the shareholding percentage and holding period; the non-resident must file a withholding tax treaty exemption/reduction application through HomeTax or with the payer's district tax office before remittance, attaching the TRC, a power of attorney, the dividend board resolution, audited financial statements or latest balance sheet, and substance documentation showing the recipient is not a conduit; if statutory 22% was erroneously withheld, a refund claim for the excess must be filed within the statutory claim period and must prove entitlement to the treaty benefits, including beneficial ownership and substantive economic activity of the non-resident shareholder
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory withholding on outbound interest and royalties is 22% aggregate (20% national plus 2% local); bilateral treaty rates generally reduce interest to 0% to 15% and royalties to 0% to 15% depending on the treaty partner and type of intangible; for an overseas PR communications firm, royalties for media software, database access rights, branding, and know-how must be distinguished from service fees, and Korea will apply source rules to reclassify fees as royalties where the payment is for the right to use confidential PR methodologies, datasets, or copyrights; treaty relief in all cases requires a valid TRC, beneficial ownership, and substantive CIGA in the treaty residence state.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File is mandatory when cross-border related-party transactions with foreign related parties exceed KRW 5 billion in the fiscal year; Master File is mandatory when the aggregate cross-border related-party transaction amount exceeds KRW 10 billion and total revenue exceeds KRW 100 billion, and the documentation must be submitted within 60 days of a request by the National Tax Service; for a Yuhan Hoesa PR agency, intercompany retainers, media buying recharges, management fees, and intellectual property royalties all count toward the threshold
approved_arm_length_methodologies: CUP, Resale Price, Cost Plus, TNMM, Profit Split
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Although Korea does not operate Gulf-style Economic Substance Regulations, Korean tax law applies substance-over-form doctrine under the Framework Act on National Taxes and the Law on the Coordination of International Tax Affairs, and treaty benefits are subject to the OECD MLI Principal Purpose Test and beneficial ownership analysis; for an overseas PR communications Yuhan Hoesa, the Core Income-Generating Activities include negotiation of client contracts, creative content development, campaign execution, media relationship management, assumption of reputational and currency risk, and final authority over spending; a Korean entity without employees, office, bank accounts, managerial capacity, or real client-facing functions will be treated as a shell, its intercompany invoices disregarded, and its income reallocated to the jurisdiction of the actual decision-makers.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion / Fraudulent Corporate Income Tax Return
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Executing a false Yuhan Hoesa corporate tax return that omits high-value overseas PR retainers, fabricates offshore marketing costs, or books personal expenses of foreign shareholders as business expenses with no supporting contracts, invoices, or performance evidence
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Punishment of Tax Evaders Act Article 3: imprisonment for not more than 5 years or a fine not exceeding three times the evaded tax, aggravated to 7 years when the evaded tax exceeds KRW 300 million; additional charges under the Framework Act on National Taxes include 20% for false non-filing, 10% for under-reporting, and 0.03% daily late-payment surcharge; the NTS may also revoke the company's electronic tax invoice registration and refer the case to the public prosecutor
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The corporate veil is pierced under judicial application of Korean Commercial Act principles and the Framework Act on National Taxes secondary liability provisions; a director who signed the fraudulent return may be personally assessed for the unpaid corporate tax and penalties, personal bank accounts and real estate may be attached, the director may be placed on the NTS tax-delinquent blacklist and subjected to an overseas travel ban, and criminal conviction can result in 5 to 7 years imprisonment and disqualification from serving as a director in South Korea

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Withholding Tax Evasion on Outbound Dividends, Interest, and Royalties
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Remitting a dividend, interest, royalty, or deemed royalty to a non-resident shareholder or overseas PR affiliate without withholding the statutory 22% tax, without obtaining treaty reduction documentation, or by masking the remittance as a non-taxable offshore settlement and recording the transaction outside the Korean corporate books
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Corporate Tax Act Articles 98, 98-2 and 98-3, together with Local Tax Act Article 103-10, impose 22% withholding tax on the gross remittance; failure to withhold makes the Yuhan Hoesa the statutory withholding agent liable for the uncollected tax, plus the Framework Act on National Taxes late-payment surcharge (0.03% per day) and an additional 10% to 20% penalty; deliberate collection and diversion of government withholding tax is punished under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act as embezzlement of national tax and carries imprisonment exposure of up to 3 years or a criminal fine in addition to full restitution
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: A director who instigated or knowingly authorized the under-withholding may be held civilly liable for the withheld tax as a fiduciary breach under Korean Commercial Act Article 399, with personal assets subject to restitution and attachment; the NTS can impose a travel ban and blacklist the director as a serious tax defaulter; because the source tax was never paid, the non-resident recipient remains taxable, and if the NTS determines the offshore arrangement was a sham, the director faces criminal indictment for embezzlement of tax and fraudulent evasion, which pierces the limited-liability shield of the company

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company Substance Failure and Transfer Pricing Mismatch
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the Korean Yuhan Hoesa as a zero-employee, zero-premises, low-capital shell that books a residual profit margin of 1% on cross-border PR services while all actual client negotiation, content production, contract execution, and risk-bearing occurs in the overseas affiliate; failing to prepare Local File/Master File when the KRW 5 billion or KRW 10 billion intercompany thresholds are met; or executing back-to-back invoices for royalty-like media data fees without a functional and risk analysis
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Law on the Coordination of International Tax Affairs permits the NTS to disregard the shell entity and re-determine the arm's-length price using any appropriate method; where reportable international transactions are not disclosed or supporting TP documentation is not produced, the NTS may impose a penalty tax related to the unreported international transaction amount, apply a 20% understatement penalty on the resulting tax deficiency, and, for refusal of evidence, use aggregate estimation; repeated or fraudulent cross-border TP manipulation is referred for criminal tax prosecution under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act with imprisonment exposure up to 5 years, aggravated to 7 years for large deficiencies
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: When a Yuhan Hoesa is only a facade and foreign shareholders exercise actual management through the directors, Korean courts may disregard separate legal personality and order the directors and beneficial shareholders to pay the company's tax liabilities out of personal assets; civil liability includes damages to the company under Korean Commercial Act Article 399 as well as unjust enrichment claims; the NTS may issue a demand against the director under the secondary tax liability regime, impose a travel ban and tax-delinquent publication, and, in aggravated cases, the director may be named as the principal offender in a criminal fraudulent-evasion indictment and sentenced to up to 7 years of imprisonment with mandatory civil restitution of the evaded tax and penalties.
